title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study (Revised)
abstract: We report a preregistered paired evaluation of a generate→validate→repair pipeline that inserts a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven configuration workflow. Using the preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference Δ = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Under the preregistered sensitivity (treat both‑missing pairs as failures; n = 200) guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015. The preregistered bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI for this sensitivity treatment (10,000 resamples, seed=1729, reproducible from archived per‑pair records) is reported in the Results section. The preregistered efficacy target (absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20) was not met. Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and accounts for the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We expand methodological, provenance, and reproducibility detail per reviewer requests and provide explicit artifact pointers and checksums in the Disclosure Statement so readers can deterministically reproduce all analyses.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and to assist NetOps at scale. Practical NetOps requires not only syntactic plausibility but demonstrable functional correctness, bounded blast radius, and end‑to‑end auditability. A common architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM proposes a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants and policy constraints; an automated repair attempts to correct violations. Prior work on tool‑assisted critique and verifier‑aided correction motivates such pipelines but lacks preregistered, paired, provenance‑complete evidence isolating the verifier effect. We therefore tested the following confirmatory research question (preregistered): Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce the rate of functional regressions and the blast radius of repairs versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded, stratified synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired confirmatory evaluation (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) isolating verifier effect with deterministic accounting; (2) complete archival of raw LLM outputs, verifier traces, provider calls, and analysis artifacts with checksums; (3) a negative but informative empirical result: modest absolute improvement (Δ≈0.016) driven by three repairs, insufficient to meet a prespecified 20‑pp efficacy threshold; (4) extensive reproducibility recipes and per‑repair provenance for deterministic cross‑checking.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven configuration and intent translation. Recent work (PreConfig; intent engines; ICNP/NetSoft papers) demonstrates effective natural‑language→IaC and intent→configuration mapping but emphasizes correctness gaps. Tool‑assisted self‑critique (e.g., CRITIC) and tool‑interactive critique studies show verifiers can reduce semantic errors in code and text—motivating verifier‑augmented NetOps pipelines. Deterministic NetOps verifiers, formal reachability tools (SymNet, ensemble verification), and IaC semantic checking provide foundations for fast functional checks. Surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent translation stress verifier coverage, repair budgets, and auditability as practical desiderata. Our study contributes a preregistered within‑task paired evaluation with full provenance and deterministic reproduction artifacts, complementing prior exploratory and benchmark work.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 fixed the confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline)). H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (power ≈ 0.80 with 200 pairs under preregistered discordant assumptions). The preregistration SHA‑256 is feba320ea2e03679...2eba3 and was archived prior to observing execution outputs.

Task generation and inclusion. We deterministically generated 200 stratified tasks using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 constrained to constructs supported by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Stratification axes: topology scale (small ≤10, medium 11–50, large 51–150) and vendor‑mix strata covering common features (BGP, OSPF, static routes, ACLs, VLANs, MTU). Tasks requiring unsupported proprietary features were automatically detected and excluded from confirmatory sampling (task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = bb87e31d...). Each task includes an initial_state, expected_final_state, a constrained allowed_touch set, and a canonical golden reference configuration (all archived).

Execution adapter and model. Experiments were executed by adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 using the declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386b...). Per preregistration, each pair used a shared initial generation candidate (the same LLM generation seeded once) that was evaluated under both conditions (baseline and guarded) to isolate the verifier effect.

Guarded pipeline semantics. Guarded episodes invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on the shared candidate. If the verifier flagged violations the pipeline invoked the automated repair subroutine once (preregistered maximum of one automated repair iteration). The verifier emits structured traces (validation_before, validation_after) containing parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count and the final_state; these structured traces form both the primary binary success indicator and the blast‑radius diagnostics archived per episode.

Missingness, retries, and stopping rules. Retry policy allowed a single automatic retry for transient provider/API failures; failure after retry was logged as a failed episode. The primary analysis followed 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed). A prespecified sensitivity ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity') treats both‑missing pairs as failures. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2); execution completed 376 episodes (24 failed episodes). The full execution manifest records provider call counts, retries, and stage counts (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. Planned episodes = 400; completed = 376; failed = 24; complete pairs included in primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810...). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3).

Primary confirmatory outcome (complete pairs n = 188). Contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e...): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0. Baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729; paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a...) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (reproducible per the recipe below).

Sensitivity (both‑missing pairs treated as failures; n = 200). Including both_missing_pairs as failures yields baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; Δ = 0.015. We computed the preregistered bootstrap percentile 95% CI for this sensitivity treatment by resampling the archived vector of 200 per‑pair outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) with replacement 10,000 times using seed = 1729 (the preregistered bootstrap parameters). The resulting bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ is [0.0, 0.0338] (see reproducibility recipe below). Exact McNemar two‑sided p (sensitivity) = 0.25.

Repair provenance and linkage. Repair invocations were rare: repair_stage_invocations = 3 (deterministic_reconciliation.json). The three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3) correspond exactly to the three repair invocations recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7...). To enable deterministic verification we provide a compact archival Table 1 (below) that copies, verbatim, the triplet entries (episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename relative to execution/provider_calls/, provider_call_sha256, final_score) extracted from execution/raw_results.jsonl. Full provider_call traces and per‑call checksums are present in the provider_calls directory in the artifact bundle and cross‑link to the raw_results entries.

Blast‑radius diagnostics. The verifier traces include parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count for every episode. These per‑episode diagnostics are the preregistered blast‑radius proxies. Repair activity was too rare (3 repairs) to support preregistered exploratory group inference on blast‑radius distributions; however the per‑episode diagnostics are archived for follow‑up analysis and representative traces are provided as examples (execution/scoring/task‑00000X‑guarded.json; SHA‑256s listed in the Disclosure).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 pp), driven by three repairs that converted verifier‑failing shared candidates into verifier‑passing final configurations (n_10 = 3). This effect is substantially below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant. Two operational mechanisms explain the modest effect: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving limited room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and repair budget — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and the pipeline allowed only one automated repair iteration, so few violations were both detected and repairable within the allotted budget.

Operational implications. Deterministic verifiers add auditability and can correct a subset of LLM mistakes; measurable operational benefit requires a nontrivial baseline error floor, verifier coverage aligned with prevalent error modes, and a sufficient repair budget (multiple iterations) to remedy complex violations. For high‑baseline correctness environments verifiers may primarily provide confidence and auditable traces rather than large absolute improvements in success rates.

Reproducibility and reviewer requests addressed. Reviewer R1 requested (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis and (b) explicit provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations. We address both here. The sensitivity CI reported above ([0.0, 0.0338]) was produced by resampling the archived 200 per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) with replacement 10,000 times using seed=1729 and taking the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles of the resampled Δ distribution; the resampling was executed by the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resample count). The three repair invocations are enumerated in Table 1, which is copied verbatim from execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls/ (artifact paths and SHA‑256s given in Disclosure). Reproducing both the bootstrap CI and the per‑repair mapping is deterministic from the archived artifacts per the provided reproduction recipe.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: single shared initial generation per pair (preregistered), limited retries, and 24 failed episodes reduced completable pairs to 188. Construct validity: success is a deterministic validator‑based binary indicator and depends on verifier coverage and the fidelity of synthetic golden configs. External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic Cornetto‑like tasks, and constrained verifier scope limit generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) limit power to detect effects smaller than preregistered threshold.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired evaluation the addition of a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration produced a small, non‑significant absolute improvement in per‑task success rate (Δ ≈ 0.016) on a stratified synthetic multi‑vendor task set using gpt‑5‑mini. The preregistered efficacy target (20‑pp) was not achieved. Repairs were rare (3) and account for the observed discordant successes. We release the preregistration, raw outputs, verifier traces, provider calls, and analysis artifacts with checksums to enable deterministic reanalysis and follow‑ups that vary baseline difficulty, verifier scope, model families, and repair budgets.

Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were excluded from final‑study evidence per the autonomy protocol. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body and includes the immutable initial master prompt reference above as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) created a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare (3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer‑requested numeric artifacts (exact per‑repair provider_call filenames and the bootstrap percentiles for alternate missingness treatments) are reproducible deterministically from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 given above) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl but were not inline enumerated in earlier manuscript snapshots; we provide a deterministic reproduction recipe and explicit artifact pointers above.
